$comment: Accepted-risk register for the npm audit / OSV gate (scripts/audit-gate.mjs).
An entry here means: the advisory is real, we have assessed it against how
this application actually uses the dependency, and we are choosing not to
block builds on it. Every entry needs a concrete reason and a review date.
Adding an entry is a security decision — it should be reviewed like one.
Kept deliberately in sync with terraform-registry-frontend's register: both
frontends carry the same react-router dependency via the shared suite-ui.

exceptions.reason: RSC-mode CSRF bypass. GitHub's advisory states outright that it 'only affects your application if you are using the unstable RSC APIs'. This app never enters that code path: it is a Vite SPA that mounts BrowserRouter in src/App.tsx for client-side routing only, and imports no server/RSC entrypoint — no unstable_* import, no react-router/server, no createStaticHandler or StaticRouterProvider anywhere in src/ (verified by grep). The advisory covers >=7.12.0 <8.3.0, so every 7.x release including the latest 7.18.2 is affected, and npm's only offered remedy is a semver-major DOWNGRADE to react-router-dom@7.11.0. Upgrading forward is not available either: react-router published 8.3.0 but react-router-dom has no 8.x line at all (latest 7.18.2, which pins react-router at exactly 7.18.2), so reaching the patched version means migrating off react-router-dom entirely across 31 source files, and @sethbacon/terraform-suite-ui itself depends on react-router 7.x. Revisit when suite-ui moves to react-router 8.x, at which point both frontends migrate together.
